evidence: Traupman 56: cibī appetentiam bonam habēre, to have a good appetite
Traupman 62: alicui (cibī) appetentiam excitāre, to give someone an appetite
terms.comment: Lack of appetite is nūlla cibī appetentia. Traupman also gives inedia for it (pp. 62, 64), but that is going without food: see fasting.
Lewis & Short s.v. appetītiō: a grasping at, a longing for something.

phrases.english: You’ve got a good appetite today!

phrases.latin: habeōque senectūtī magnam grātiam, quae mihi sermōnis aviditātem auxit, pōtiōnis et cibī sustulit
phrases.english: and I am very grateful to old age, which has increased my appetite for conversation and taken away my appetite for food and drink

sources: Lewis & Short: appetentia
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. appetite.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 56, 62, 149, 151.
